title: Taller, kindest, just like Mom: comparisons
objectives: Compare two things with mas ... kaysa
Say two things are equal with kasing- and alike with gaya ng / tulad ng

grammar.title: Mas ... kaysa: comparing two things
grammar.explanation:
To compare, put mas (more) before the adjective: 'Mas mura ito' — this is cheaper. To name what you're comparing against, add kaysa: kaysa sa + common noun, kaysa kay + personal name.

'Mas matangkad si Ben kaysa kay Carlo.' — Ben is taller than Carlo.
'Mas masarap ang mangga kaysa sa saging.' — Mangoes are tastier than bananas.

In relaxed speech you'll also hear kaysa dropped to plain sa ('Mas matangkad si Ben sa akin') or kesa — all fine, but learn the full kaysa sa / kaysa kay pattern first.

The 'less' direction usually flips the adjective rather than using a 'less' word: instead of 'less tall', say mas pandak (shorter). To soften a comparison: medyo (somewhat) — 'Medyo mas mahal dito.'

examples.tl: Mas mura ang gulay sa palengke kaysa sa supermarket.
examples.en: Vegetables are cheaper at the market than at the supermarket.

examples.tl: Mas matanda ako kaysa sa kapatid ko, pero mas matangkad siya!
examples.en: I'm older than my sibling, but he's taller!

examples.tl: Mas gusto ko ang kape kaysa sa tsaa.
examples.en: I like coffee more than tea.

grammar.title: Pinaka-: the superlative
grammar.explanation:
The superlative is a prefix: pinaka- + adjective (the ma- usually stays): pinakamaganda (most beautiful), pinakamatalino (smartest), pinakamura (cheapest), pinakamalaki (biggest).

'Si Ana ang pinakamatalino sa klase.' — Ana is the smartest in the class. Notice the frame: ang pinaka- phrase names the champion, and sa + group tells you the field of competition (sa klase, sa pamilya, sa lahat — of all).

A very common conversational move puts the pinaka- phrase up front with ang: 'Ito ang pinakamasarap na adobo sa Maynila!' — This is the tastiest adobo in Manila! Don't forget the linker (-ng/na) when the superlative modifies a noun: pinakamasarap NA adobo, pinakamalaking kuwarto.

examples.tl: Ito ang pinakamurang cellphone sa tindahan.
examples.en: This is the cheapest cellphone in the store.

examples.tl: Si Lola ang pinakamabait sa pamilya namin.
examples.en: Grandma is the kindest in our family.

examples.tl: Ano ang pinakamataas na bundok sa Pilipinas?
examples.en: What is the tallest mountain in the Philippines?

grammar.title: Kasing-, gaya ng, tulad ng: as ... as, and 'like'
grammar.explanation:
To say two things are EQUAL, prefix kasing- to the adjective root (the ma- falls off): kasingtangkad (as tall as), kasingganda (as beautiful as), kasingbait (as kind as). The standard of comparison takes ng-marking: ni before names, ng before nouns:

'Kasingtangkad ako ni Ben.' — I'm as tall as Ben.
'Hindi kasingtamis ng mangga ang papaya.' — Papaya isn't as sweet as mango.

To say 'like/similar to' without an adjective, use gaya ng or tulad ng (they're interchangeable): gaya ng nanay ko (like my mom), tulad ng sabi ko (like I said). Before names: gaya ni / tulad ni.

'Gaya ng tatay ko, mahilig ako sa basketball.' — Like my dad, I'm into basketball. Related and very handy: mukhang + adjective/noun = 'looks like/seems': 'Mukhang pagod ka' — you look tired. 'Mukhang uulan' — looks like rain. And magkamukha = (two people) look alike: 'Magkamukha kayo ng kapatid mo!'

examples.en: His mom is as kind as he is.

examples.tl: Tulad ng lola ko, madaldal din ako.
examples.en: Like my grandma, I'm also talkative.

examples.tl: Magkamukha talaga kayo ng ate mo.
examples.en: You and your big sister really look alike.

example.tl: Mas malamig sa Baguio kaysa sa Maynila.
example.en: It's colder in Baguio than in Manila.

vocab.note: kaysa sa + noun, kaysa kay + name

example.tl: Mas mabilis ang MRT kaysa sa bus.
example.en: The MRT is faster than the bus.

example.tl: Ito ang pinakamasarap na halo-halo dito.
example.en: This is the most delicious halo-halo here.

vocab.note: kasing + adjective root: kasingtangkad ni Ben

example.tl: Kasingtangkad na ng tatay niya ang anak.
example.en: The son is now as tall as his dad.

example.tl: Gaya ng nanay ko, mahilig akong magluto.
example.en: Like my mom, I love to cook.

example.tl: Tulad ng sabi ko, darating ako nang maaga.
example.en: Like I said, I'll arrive early.

example.tl: Matangkad ang bagong kasamahan namin.
example.en: Our new workmate is tall.

vocab.note: can be teasing; maliit is gentler

example.tl: Mas pandak ako kaysa sa kapatid ko.
example.en: I'm shorter than my sibling.

example.tl: Payat siya noong bata siya.
example.en: He was thin when he was a kid.

example.tl: Mataba ang pusa namin. Kain nang kain!
example.en: Our cat is fat. It just eats and eats!

example.tl: Guwapo raw ang bagong titser. Totoo ba?
example.en: They say the new teacher is handsome. Is it true?

example.tl: Mahaba ang buhok ni Carla.
example.en: Carla's hair is long.

example.tl: Kulot ang buhok ng anak nila.
example.en: Their child's hair is curly.

example.tl: Tuwid at maikli ang buhok niya ngayon.
example.en: Her hair is straight and short now.

example.tl: Hugasan mo ang mukha mo. May sauce!
example.en: Wash your face. There's sauce on it!

vocab.note: mukha + linker: mukhang pagod, mukhang uulan

example.tl: Mukhang masarap ang niluluto mo!
example.en: What you're cooking looks delicious!

example.tl: Magkamukha ang magkapatid na iyon.
example.en: Those siblings look alike.

example.tl: Pinakamasipag si Nena sa opisina namin.
example.en: Nena is the most hardworking in our office.

example.tl: Medyo tamad ako tuwing Linggo.
example.en: I'm a bit lazy on Sundays.

example.tl: Matalino at masipag ang estudyanteng iyon.
example.en: That student is smart and hardworking.

example.tl: Masayahin ang lola ko kahit matanda na siya.
example.en: My grandma is cheerful even though she's old now.

example.tl: Mahiyain ang anak ko sa mga bago niyang kaklase.
example.en: My child is shy around her new classmates.

example.tl: Ang daldal mo naman! Makinig ka muna.
example.en: You're so chatty! Listen first.

example.tl: Tahimik siya sa klase pero madaldal sa bahay.
example.en: She's quiet in class but chatty at home.

example.tl: Palakaibigan ang mga kapitbahay namin.
example.en: Our neighbors are friendly.

vocab.note: suplado for a man; casual Manila word

example.tl: Hindi siya suplada; mahiyain lang talaga siya.
example.en: She's not a snob; she's really just shy.

vocab.note: mahilig sa + noun; mahilig + linker + verb

example.tl: Mahilig ako sa mga lumang kanta.
example.en: I'm into old songs.

example.tl: Medyo mahal dito, pero masarap.
example.en: It's a bit pricey here, but delicious.

dialogue.title: Which sister is which?
dialogue.context: Nina shows her officemate Paulo a photo from her sister's graduation, and Paulo tries to guess who's who.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.tl: Uy, sino ito sa picture? Kapatid mo ba?
lines.en: Hey, who's this in the picture? Your sister?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.tl: Oo, sila ang dalawa kong kapatid, sina Joy at Karen.
lines.en: Yes, those are my two sisters, Joy and Karen.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.tl: Naku, magkamukha kayong tatlo! Sino ang mas matanda?
lines.en: Wow, the three of you look alike! Who's older?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.tl: Si Joy, iyong may mahabang kulot na buhok. Mas matanda siya sa akin.
lines.en: Joy, the one with long curly hair. She's older than me.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.tl: At si Karen iyong matangkad na may tuwid na buhok?
lines.en: And Karen is the tall one with straight hair?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.tl: Tama! Pinakamatangkad siya sa aming tatlo, kahit siya ang bunso.
lines.en: Right! She's the tallest of us three, even though she's the youngest.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.en: Do you all have the same personality?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.tl: Hindi! Madaldal ako, pero tahimik at mahiyain si Karen.
lines.en: No! I'm chatty, but Karen is quiet and shy.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.tl: Si Joy naman ang pinakamasipag sa amin. Gaya ng nanay namin, mahilig siyang magluto.
lines.en: Joy is the most hardworking of us. Like our mom, she loves to cook.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.tl: Mukhang masaya ang pamilya ninyo, ah.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.tl: Oo naman! Pero ako pa rin ang pinakamagandang kapatid, ha!
lines.en: Of course! But I'm still the prettiest sibling, okay!

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.tl: Hindi ako sasagot diyan. Baka magalit ang mga kapatid mo!
lines.en: I'm not answering that. Your sisters might get mad!

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'Ben is taller than Carlo'?
choices: Mas matangkad si Ben kaysa kay Carlo.
exercises.explain: Mas + adjective for the comparison, kaysa kay before a personal name.

exercises.prompt: Mas mura ang gulay sa palengke ___ sa supermarket. (than at the supermarket)
exercises.explain: Kaysa sa + common noun: cheaper than at the supermarket.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'the smartest in the class'?
exercises.explain: Pinaka- forms the superlative; sa klase names the group being compared.

exercises.prompt: Si Lola ang ___mabait sa pamilya namin. (Grandma is the kindest in our family.)
exercises.explain: The superlative prefix pinaka- attaches to the adjective: pinakamabait.
Kasing- + root expresses equality, with the standard marked by ni before a name.

exercises.prompt: What happens to the adjective in kasing- forms? (maganda → ?)
exercises.explain: The ma- prefix drops before kasing-: kasingganda, kasingtangkad, kasingbait.

exercises.tl: Mas matanda si Joy kaysa kay Karen, pero mas matangkad si Karen.
choices: Joy is older; Karen is taller.
Karen is older; Joy is taller.
Joy is both older and taller.
exercises.explain: Mas matanda si Joy (Joy is older) kaysa kay Karen; pero mas matangkad si Karen (but Karen is taller).

exercises.prompt: ___ ng tatay ko, mahilig ako sa basketball. (Like my dad, I'm into basketball.)
exercises.explain: Gaya ng and tulad ng both mean 'like/similar to' and are interchangeable here.

exercises.prompt: Your friend arrives yawning with messy hair. The natural comment is:
exercises.explain: Mukhang + adjective = 'you look/seem...': mukhang pagod ka, you look tired.

exercises.prompt: This is the cheapest cellphone in the store.
exercises.answer: Ito ang pinakamurang cellphone sa tindahan.
accept: Ito ang pinakamurang cellphone sa tindahan
Ang pinakamurang cellphone sa tindahan ay ito
Ito ang pinakamurang cellphone dito sa tindahan
exercises.explain: Pinaka- + mura + linker -ng before the noun: pinakamurang cellphone.

exercises.prompt: Tahimik siya sa opisina, pero madaldal siya sa mga kaibigan niya.
exercises.answer: He is quiet at the office, but talkative with his friends.
accept: He is quiet at the office, but talkative with his friends
She is quiet at the office but chatty with her friends
He's quiet at the office but talkative around his friends
exercises.explain: Tahimik = quiet, madaldal = talkative; pero contrasts the two settings.

exercises.prompt: I like coffee more than tea.
exercises.answer: Mas gusto ko ang kape kaysa sa tsaa.
accept: Mas gusto ko ang kape kaysa sa tsaa
Mas gusto ko ng kape kaysa sa tsaa
Mas gusto ko ang kape kesa sa tsaa
exercises.explain: Mas gusto ko + the preferred thing, kaysa sa + the runner-up.

exercises.prompt: Someone describes a new neighbor: 'Hindi siya suplada; mahiyain lang siya.' What are they saying?
choices: She's not a snob — she's just shy.
exercises.explain: Hindi suplada rejects 'snobbish'; mahiyain lang (just shy) offers the kinder explanation, with lang from Unit 5.

exercises.prompt: Describe someone cheerful by nature: ___ ang lola ko kahit matanda na siya.
exercises.hint: The -in suffix on masaya means 'tends to be'.
exercises.explain: Masayahin means characteristically cheerful — a personality trait, not just a mood (masaya).
